speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) how stockpiled food is drawn down on; and (b) whether steps are taken to avoid food wastage in the process.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) how frequently are food items in national stockpiles replaced to ensure nutritional value is not diminished; (b) whether the food items released from stockpiles can still be sold or distributed to reduce food wastage; (c) whether the cost of freezing the stockpiles in sub-zero temperature warehouses is borne by food suppliers; and (d) if so, how are they compensated.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in respect of the current national food stockpiling (a) by whom and how are stockpiling decisions made on food products that are not mandated by law; and (b) whether alternative proteins are currently stockpiled in addition to traditional proteins.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in respect of the cold rooms used for national food stockpiling (a) what are the measures to ensure an uninterrupted power supply; (b) whether such measures are legally mandated; and (c) whether the Ministry conducts regular inspections to ensure compliance.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment whether the cost of prevailing food supply prices are taken into consideration when deciding whether food which are stockpiled should be drawn down to mitigate any sudden or anomalous spikes food supply prices.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Our stockpiles are not intended as a mechanism to influence food prices.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Singapore Food Agency (SFA) conducts regular inspections of our food stockpiles to ensure compliance with requirements.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: Also, what are the considerations in terms of sustaining the freshness of the food that is in the stockpile?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I just want to assure the Member that our stockpiles provide a critical buffer, especially when you think about food resilience in Singapore and how we may need to draw down in times of crises.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As Minister Grace Fu shared a few days ago, we have now embarked on the Singapore Food Story 2, in which the stockpile is just one of four pillars.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will often try to diversify and rely on our local imports first, to ensure that we are food-resilient, before drawing on the stockpiles.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: There is also "Grow Local", in which we want to ensure that we have enough local supply before we draw down from the food stockpiles.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Lastly, we are now embarking on a new pillar, "Global Partnerships", in which we are working with other countries to ensure food resilience.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, where stockpiling is concerned, we draw down only when it is most critical.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As I mentioned in my reply earlier on, SFA conducts regular inspections to ensure that our food is safe, they are not expired and more importantly, that we do regular churns as well in the system to ensure that there is adequate, safe supply of food in our system.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In doing do, we want to minimise food wastage, to ensure where possible, we try to get towards zero food waste.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I want to assure the Member that food waste is kept to a minimum in this regard.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the stockpiling of food through the private sector, today, we have the Minimum Stockholding Requirement (MSR).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, the rest of it is Government stockpile.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I cannot reveal too much, as it involves national security concerns, as the Member may be familiar with.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Our stockpiles are in consideration of not just the disruptions that could occur in the short term, such as pandemics or other forms of disruption, but also long-drawn situations where you have decisions, such as war blockades and other matters.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Rest assured that the Government does its best to minimise impact to food prices, to minimise impact to the private sector, but at the same time keeping food safe in our stockpiles.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I note the Senior Minister of State's assurances that there is zero food wastage, but he also shared that there is churn to make sure that the food is kept fresh and suitable for consumption.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, my question is whether he can share a little bit more in terms of what are the strategies to ensure zero food wastage?

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Because we do not want to also impact the market; so, are the food used for community purposes, for example?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In my reply, I spoke about how we work with the private sector, commercial operators, where this is also quite efficient.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Through them, there is offtake, there are ways in which we can minimise food wastage.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As food expires, you also want to – I would not say on the very last date – but there are ways to churn them through the system.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think that is important because that is an efficient market measure, in which we churn and at the same time, not impact food supply and food prices here.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: There are occasions in which we may also dispose of them through food donations, but those are typically on a large scale, like humanitarian efforts, for example.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, those are things that we do sometimes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At the same time, how we dispose and how we do that, I cannot give you too much detail again because of national security concerns.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I want to assure the Member that we work towards zero waste.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I am not going to say zero waste today, but we are working towards zero waste as we minimise some of the food churn.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I understand that the cost of prevailing food supply prices are currently not taken into consideration at this point in time, but whether moving forward, we can take this into consideration and consider working closely with the Ministry of Trade and Industry?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While I understand that we want to ensure sufficient food supplies for food security purposes, we also want to take care of our merchants and hawkers in trying to mitigate their operating cost.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And there has been feedback that there has been a sudden surge in some of the protein items, for example, like chicken, which, as a result, they are deliberating whether to transfer this cost to the consumers.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As a result, it will invariably become a concern in terms of the cost of living.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Having said that, as I said, it is really about stockpiling.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We churn out through the commercial players, aiming not to disrupt the market.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think that is one of the key considerations for us.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I just want to assure the Member that we do our best, but at the same time as well, let us keep the two separate: stockpiling and food price mechanism.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: I note that no alternative proteins are being stockpiled now.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: My second supplementary question is, in my Parliamentary Question, I do not think I got an answer on the measures of sites and the audits on the sites available, especially for frozen food.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: Will you be looking at uninterruptible power supplies and how often will you do the audits?

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: Because, as you mentioned, with the MSR coming on board, there will be more sites allocated for such stockpiling measures.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, those are regular audits to ensure that our food supply is adequate and at the same time as well, safe.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the locations, I cannot disclose where they are, but I can assure the Member as well that as we pick these locations, we look into storage capability standards, making sure that they are able to stock our food stockpiles in a safe manner without having to worry about supply interruptions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I think for Singapore, touch wood, we have been quite okay with our energy and power supplies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I am quite sure with some of these warehouses, like the one I visited, for example, they have such measures in place because we are not the only customer that they have.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: They are also managing it for other multinational firms and local firms as well who require such food stockpiles.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For locations that we pick, I think we have to ensure that they are of sufficient standards.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And I can assure the Member that is the case.
